subject: Re: Neptune Health - encryption approach + SOC 2 gaps (post-demo follow-up)
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Emma Liu <emma@neptunehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Sep 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Neptune demo follow-up — encryption posture & SOC 2 status

Hi Emma — thanks again for the demo earlier today. Quick recap and next steps from our side so we can align on security/compliance before procurement: 

- SOC 2: you mentioned an audit in progress with an expected report in Q4. Can you confirm scope (Type I vs Type II) and which AWS accounts/environments are in scope?
- Encryption at rest: you referenced using AWS KMS. Do you use AWS-managed keys, Neptune-managed CMKs, or a customer BYOK model?
- HSM requirement: is Neptune expecting HSM-backed key material for vendors, or will a KMS CMK with strict key policy suffice?
- In-transit: TLS termination points (edge/load balancer vs app) — any special interceptors/mtls?
- Vendor questionnaire: want to kick off our standard vendor security questionnaire so we can capture controls, evidence, and any requested exceptions. I'll attach our template if helpful.

Proposed next steps: 
1) If you can share the SOC 2 target date and the Neptune_Security_Overview.pdf (or SOC 2 bridge letter), we'll start our internal procurement/security review.
2) Please share a sample KMS key policy or a statement on whether you require BYOK/HSM.
3) If helpful, schedule a 30-min technical deep-dive next week (we'll include our infra/security engineer).

I'll loop Marissa and Karthik for the intake — they can advise on evidence we will need for the legal and infra teams.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
(415) 555-0139

Attachments referenced: redwood_vendor_qs_v1.xlsx (attached in a follow-up)
From: Emma Liu <emma@neptunehealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: David Park <david.park@neptunehealth.com>, security@neptunehealth.com
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Neptune demo follow-up — encryption posture & SOC 2 status

Thanks Logan — great conversation yesterday. Answers below and attaching a short overview. Attachment: Neptune_Security_Overview.pdf (summary + contacts).

- SOC 2: We are currently undergoing a Type II audit for our core patient platform; report expected 2027-11-15 (controls in production since 2026-12-01). We can provide the auditor contact and a bridge letter once available.
- Encryption at rest: We use AWS KMS with customer-managed CMKs in our production account (not AWS-managed). Keys are created in our AWS account; we do not currently do BYOK exports of raw key material outside AWS.
- HSM: We rely on AWS CloudHSM-managed keys for higher-assurance workloads. For third-party vendors, we typically ask for support for CMK key policies that restrict usage to verified principals and for the ability to provide key usage logs.
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+ for all service-to-service traffic; mTLS for internal services. External vendor traffic terminates at our ingress layer and is proxied to downstream services — we can share the ingress diagram in the next packet.

For the vendor questionnaire: please send your template — we'd like to complete it and return within 5 business days. If you need any KMS policy examples, ask David (copied).

Best,
Emma Liu
Security Program Manager
Neptune Health

Forwarding Neptune's reply — key points below:
- SOC 2 Type II expected 2027-11-15; controls in production since 2026-12-01.
- They use customer-managed CMKs in their AWS account; no BYOK export of raw key material today. They also use CloudHSM for higher-assurance workloads.
- They expect vendors to support key policy restrictions and provide key-usage logs.
- They will complete our vendor questionnaire in ~5 business days if we send it.

Requesting: can you both review and confirm what evidence we need for procurement and whether Neptune's CMK/CloudHSM approach satisfies typical enterprise requirements? Also confirm if we need to open a QSA or legal exception for the BYOK gap (they don't export key material).

I attached our redwood_vendor_qs_v1.xlsx to this thread (template) — please fill the security/evidence checklist items we should expect back from Neptune and mark any items that will require additional engineering work (e.g., proof of key-usage logging to our audit pipeline).

Logan
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2027 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Neptune demo follow-up — encryption posture & SOC 2 status

Thanks for the forward. Initial read: Neptune's posture is acceptable for most of our enterprise customers — CMKs in vendor account + CloudHSM for sensitive workloads is a standard pattern. A few asks for the checklist: 

- Evidence items to request from Neptune:
  - SOC 2 bridge letter now and final Type II report when available (Doc request).
  - KMS key policy sample(s) for the CMKs used with our integration. We need to validate that the key policy allows explicit principals and denies broad access.
  - CloudHSM usage details and attestation of HSM-backed key creation for any high-risk PHI flows.
  - Key usage logs (CloudTrail) covering Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey calls for the keys used with Redwood traffic — 90 days minimum to start.
  - Network diagram showing ingress TLS termination and vendor-proxy boundaries.

- Technical impacts for Redwood:
  - If Neptune refuses any form of key export/BYOK, we need to confirm whether our runtime can perform envelope encryption where Neptune manages the CMK and we maintain tenant-level data separation. That is supported but we need an infra engineering sync to validate telemetry and logging.
  - If they require HSM-backed vendor keys for all PHI, that may require a scoped runbook for handling HSM-backed key rotations and additional key access controls.

Next actions I recommend:
1) Send redwood_vendor_qs_v1.xlsx to Neptune (Logan, looks like you've attached it) and ask for the documents above.
2) Karthik: can you provision ~30 min tomorrow with our infra security engineer (Ilya) to map any telemetry gaps (CloudTrail ingestion, KMS key policy evaluation)?
3) I'll flag any contract language that looks like an exception (BYOK/export demands or HSM-mandates) and loop legal early.

Marissa Cole
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
